title: A thalamocortical circuit encoding deviations from sensory history.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the paper's Zenodo deposit (record 20267242, 'Code and Source Data for A thalamo-cortical circuit for contrastive coding of sensory history', 17.4 MB, CC-BY-4.0). Opened all 14 Excel workbooks (103 sheets, 903 non-empty rows in total, largest single sheet 27 rows) and all 6 NumPy arrays: PCA projections (100 cross-validation iterations x 10 principal components x 8 stimuli x 30-40 timepoints), pairwise Euclidean distances (100 x 8 x 8), and targeted-dimensionality-reduction regression weights (LP: 75 iterations x 1828 units x 7 task variables; ACC: 100 x 148 x 7). Read both deposit READMEs and listed the 11 Python analysis scripts. Searched Zenodo, Dryad, DANDI and the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.11.16.623977v2) for any raw data deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Animal and session counts (24 mice behaving, 22 in the psychometric analysis, 17 imaging sessions in 5 mice task-engaged, 13 sessions in 5 mice passive, 9 ACC sessions in 3 mice) come from the bioRxiv preprint text; the Science version is paywalled (science.org returned HTTP 403) so its own data-availability statement was not read. The preprint's statement says only 'All data necessary for evaluating the conclusions are available in the main text or the supplementary materials'.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record 20267242 downloaded without login, 17.4 MB zip, CC-BY-4.0; md5 matched the record metadata. Checked in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. No trial-level outcome exists anywhere. The mouse's choice, hit/miss and the trial-by-trial stimulus difference survive only as pre-averaged group means and standard errors inside figure panels (e.g. 'P(ChooseR) by signed coherence x |Delta Dir|' is an 8-column grid of means, not rows of trials). Any model target would have to be reconstructed from data that was never deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No per-trial stimulus features (direction, coherence, previous-trial values) and no per-bouton calcium traces. The only unit-level object, a 1828 x 7 array of regression weights, carries no mouse, session or bouton identifier, so rows cannot be grouped or joined to anything.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated where they exist: probabilities, seconds, and 'AU' (arbitrary units) for principal-component projections, documented in both READMEs. Checked in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, and this is the decisive one. Largest table in the whole deposit is 27 rows (per-mouse hit rate, Fig 1C). 903 non-empty rows exist in total but are spread over 103 heterogeneous figure panels with different row meanings, so they cannot be stacked into one table. Checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 17.4 MB compressed, 18.4 MB uncompressed; loads in under a second on a laptop. Checked in the files.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 27-row and 29-row behavioural sheets are consistent with the preprint's 22-24 mice, and the LP array's 1828 units is plausible for pooled axonal boutons. Cannot cross-check against the Science text, which is paywalled.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL for the only unit-level data. The targeted-dimensionality-reduction weights and the principal-component projections are outputs of the authors' own regression and dimensionality reduction, not measurements; modelling them would mean fitting their analysis rather than the neural activity. The physical measurement (fluorescence traces) was never deposited.

integration.partner_dataset: International Brain Laboratory brain-wide map (trial-level mouse visual-decision behaviour and electrophysiology)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: this deposit has no trial, session, animal or unit identifier that would join to any external resource, so the integration is decoration.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the paper's own published effect, that the psychometric slope rises with |Delta Dir| (the difference in motion direction between consecutive trials); only the already-averaged panel values are available, so it cannot be independently recovered.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless with 27 rows per sheet and no trial labels.
controls.external_validation: Related higher-order-thalamus decision datasets exist (e.g. the 2026 Neuron paper on history-based decision-making, and the International Brain Laboratory data), but nothing in this deposit can be aligned to them.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is possible: the deposit supports only re-plotting the paper's own figures, because every value in it is already averaged across trials or is the output of the authors' own regression.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the current visual stimulus and the recent trial history to predict which way a mouse will choose.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input per example: the motion strength and direction a mouse sees on one trial, plus what it saw and chose on the previous few trials. Number of trial-level examples actually available: zero; only 27 per-mouse summary values.
plain_idea.predict: Intended output: the mouse's left/right choice (or whether it repeats its last choice) on the current trial, which is measured directly by the lick/turn response in the behavioural rig. That per-trial record was not deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Systems neuroscientists studying how expectations shape perception would want a model that separates stimulus-driven from history-driven choices, and the paper shows that a specific brain pathway carries exactly that signal; the published data cannot support building it.

ml_idea: The attractive project was: predict a mouse's trial-by-trial choice from current motion evidence plus recent sensory and reward history, then ask whether population activity in the thalamus-to-prefrontal (LP-ACC) pathway adds predictive power beyond behaviour alone, and whether optogenetic silencing selectively removes the history term. All three parts need trial-level behaviour and bouton-level calcium traces. The deposit contains neither, so the idea is not executable from this paper's public data.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not estimated: the whole deposit is 18.4 MB uncompressed and every file was loaded into pandas and NumPy on this laptop in a few seconds. Size was never the problem; content was.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the largest sheet and count its rows. It has 27, which is 1/55th of the checklist's minimum, and it took about two minutes to find out.

verdict_reason: Data downloads cleanly under CC-BY but is figure source data only: 103 panel sheets of pre-averaged means and standard errors (largest 27 rows) plus derived principal-component and regression outputs. No trial-level behaviour and no calcium traces, so A2, A3, A5 and A8 all fail.
